mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which increases consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < PAYEMS growth rate for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In the identified regime, the correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline is not predictive of SPX 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% month-over-month indicates accelerating economic demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During this regime, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 5-day risk-free rate (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months suggests the Fed may maintain current rates, reducing discount rate expectations and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In this regime, SPX 20-day returns are not higher than the 20-day Treasury bill rate (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the RSAFS exceeds 10% in a single month, it indicates a large surprise contraction in credit demand, which typically precedes a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In this regime, SPX 60-day returns do not show a significant negative relationship with the RSAFS monthly change (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising housing starts (not directly observable in the provided catalog but as a domain extension, we consider HOUST as a proxy for housing activity) coupled with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) form a labor market recovery signal that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for two consecutive months and UNRATE decreases over the same period
regime_hint: rebound in housing and labor markets
failure_condition: The interaction of HOUST and UNRATE is not predictive of SPX 20-day returns (R-squared < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for 6 months suggests the Fed is likely to hold rates steady, which reduces discount rate expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days in a steady-state economy.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not higher than the risk-free rate in this regime (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by at least 3% in the same month indicates weakening demand and cost pressures that often precede a bearish S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < prev and CPIAUCSL < prev by >= 3%
failure_condition: The combined effect of INDPRO and CPIAUCSL is not predictive of SPX 20-day returns (p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test).
